library_preparation_preflight.summary: ai.djl.huggingface:tokenizers' native JNI binary (CharSpan) already runs clean in this repo's native-image harness as a transitive dep of langchain4j-embeddings-all-minilm-l6-v2, with no extra Maven dependency, Docker image, or env/system property. No deterministic setup is needed; the only risk is the generated test defaulting to a network-based tokenizer load.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Construct the HuggingFaceTokenizer from a small local tokenizer.json bundled as a test resource (e.g. via HuggingFaceTokenizer.newInstance(Path)) rather than HuggingFaceTokenizer.newInstance("<model-name>"), which downloads from HuggingFace Hub at runtime and would make the test network-dependent and flaky. This mirrors the working pattern already in tests/src/dev.langchain4j/langchain4j-embeddings-all-minilm-l6-v2, which bundles its own tokenizer.json instead of fetching one. No DJL_CACHE_DIR or other env var is needed since the native library ships inside the tokenizers jar for common platforms (confirmed working on this CI's Linux x86_64).
risks: DJL bundles native binaries in the jar for common platforms (linux-x86_64, osx-x86_64/aarch64, win-x86_64); if CI ever runs on an uncommon architecture, a runtime native-library download could be triggered — not expected on this repo's standard Linux x86_64 runners.
If the generated test ignores the guidance and loads a tokenizer by name instead of from a bundled resource, it will depend on live network access to huggingface.co at test time.
